adversarial_tests.claim: Independent receipt verification compares every field of a settlement receipt against the authoritative record — the stored request, the stored signed approval, and the gated store-history entry — and additionally verifies the receipt's signature under the engine's instance secret. A single-field alteration of the stated object, the prestate digest, the sequence number, or the approval digest is rejected; the poststate digest, already bound in v0.1, stays rejected; and a field-perfect receipt re-signed with the published key is rejected on its signature.

controls.expected: The receipt exactly as issued verifies against the authoritative record (the control proving the A1 setup itself is valid).
controls.name: untouched_receipt_verifies

controls.expected: A receipt altered in exactly one field — the stated object (effect.object) — is rejected by independent verification (verifier code: effect_object_mismatch). In v0.1 this alteration verified; the field is now compared against the authoritative record, not taken on trust.
controls.name: altered_stated_object_rejected

controls.expected: A receipt altered in exactly one field — the prestate digest (effect.prestate_digest) — is rejected by independent verification (verifier code: prestate_digest_mismatch). In v0.1 this alteration verified; the field is now compared against the authoritative record, not taken on trust.
controls.name: altered_prestate_digest_rejected

controls.expected: A receipt altered in exactly one field — the sequence number (seq) — is rejected by independent verification (verifier code: seq_mismatch). In v0.1 this alteration verified; the field is now compared against the authoritative record, not taken on trust.
controls.name: altered_sequence_number_rejected

controls.expected: A receipt altered in exactly one field — the approval digest (approval_digest) — is rejected by independent verification (verifier code: approval_digest_mismatch). In v0.1 this alteration verified; the field is now compared against the authoritative record, not taken on trust.
controls.name: altered_approval_digest_rejected

controls.expected: A receipt altered in exactly one field — the poststate digest (effect.poststate_digest) — already bound in v0.1; it must stay rejected — is rejected by independent verification (verifier code: no_matching_gated_effect). In v0.1 this alteration verified; the field is now compared against the authoritative record, not taken on trust.
controls.name: altered_poststate_digest_rejected
controls.observed: verify_receipt(altered the poststate digest (effect.poststate_digest) — already bound in v0.1; it must stay rejected) = (False, no_matching_gated_effect)

controls.expected: A receipt whose every field matches the authoritative record but whose signature was recomputed under the PUBLISHED fixture key is rejected on the signature (receipt_signature_invalid): v0.3 receipts are signed under the engine's per-instance secret, so forgery rejection is a signature property, not only a ledger property. In v0.1/v0.2 the published key was the system's only signing material and a signature authenticated nothing.
controls.name: resigned_with_published_key_rejected

adversarial_tests.claim: Revocation enforcement walks the declared ancestry: after an upstream request is revoked, new reliance on it through any declared intermediate is refused with dependency_revoked — enforcement now matches the transitive detection the engine already reported. Unrelated authorized activity is unaffected, and the structural impossibility of a declared cycle is stated, not papered over.

controls.expected: Detection is unchanged from v0.1: dependents_of(A) reports both B and C, and both derived statuses read contested_revoked_ancestry. The v0.1 defect was never detection — it was enforcement stopping at the direct edge.
controls.name: transitive_detection_reports_revoked_ancestry

controls.expected: A new action declaring dependence on C (two declared intermediates from A), executed after A was revoked, is refused (dependency_revoked): enforcement walks the declared ancestry to the revoked request. In v0.1 this reliance was admitted whenever C (two declared intermediates from A) was not itself the revoked request.
controls.name: reliance_through_c_refused
controls.observed: execute(reliance via C (two declared intermediates from A)) = refusal:dependency_revoked

controls.expected: A new action declaring dependence on B (one declared intermediate from A), executed after A was revoked, is refused (dependency_revoked): enforcement walks the declared ancestry to the revoked request. In v0.1 this reliance was admitted whenever B (one declared intermediate from A) was not itself the revoked request.
controls.name: reliance_through_b_refused
controls.observed: execute(reliance via B (one declared intermediate from A)) = refusal:dependency_revoked

controls.expected: A new action declaring dependence on A itself (the direct edge — already refused in v0.1), executed after A was revoked, is refused (dependency_revoked): enforcement walks the declared ancestry to the revoked request. In v0.1 this reliance was admitted whenever A itself (the direct edge — already refused in v0.1) was not itself the revoked request.
controls.name: direct_reliance_on_revoked_refused
controls.observed: execute(reliance via A itself (the direct edge — already refused in v0.1)) = refusal:dependency_revoked

controls.expected: An authorized action declaring no dependence on the revoked chain still executes after the revocation; the ancestry walk refuses reliance on revoked authority, not unrelated work.
controls.name: unrelated_action_admitted

controls.expected: STRUCTURAL, on the record: a declared dependence cycle cannot be constructed with this kit's API, because a request_id is a content digest over depends_on — closing a cycle would require a hash fixed point. The pair built against a placeholder does not close (the computed id differs from the placeholder it would have to equal), and iterated self-dependence reaches no fixed point. There is therefore no cycle-revocation behavior to claim, in either direction.
controls.name: declared_cycle_unconstructible

controls.expected: After the engine's state is carried through the export/import dump/load into a fresh Engine (the restart carriage of the examination record), enforcement is identical: reliance through C and direct reliance on A are both refused, and C's derived status still reads contested_revoked_ancestry. In v0.1 the through-C reliance was admitted after the same carriage.
controls.name: restart_carriage_preserves_enforcement

adversarial_tests.claim: Authorization in v0.3 is a property of registered principals, checked where it bites: approve() admits only a registered, active approver presenting a valid proof; execute() re-checks the approver's current authorization, so withdrawal after approval blocks the effect; propose() authenticates the actor's proof over the exact request; sensitive reads require the reader role and are audited, served or refused. The compromised-but-valid-credential case is not claimed: it is a standing limitation, stated in the engine's strength statement, not silently absorbed into these passes.

controls.expected: An approval presented under the string 'arbitrary-unauthorized-string' — not a registered principal — is refused at approve() (approver_not_authorized) and records nothing. In v0.2 this exact string was accepted as an approver and its approval executed (Nov 9 comparison, V8 leg B).
controls.name: arbitrary_string_approver_refused

controls.expected: An approval by a registered approver, followed by withdrawal of that approver's authorization before execution, refuses at execute() (approver_no_longer_authorized): execute() re-checks the approver's CURRENT authorization, so a standing approval from a withdrawn approver authorizes no effect. In v0.2 the fixture had no approver-authorization concept at all (V8 leg B: NOT_SUPPORTED).
controls.name: withdrawn_approver_execution_refused

controls.expected: A proposal whose actor is an unregistered bare string ('compromised-anyone', the exact assertion the Nov 9 V9 leg B executed under in v0.2), and a proposal under a registered actor's name with an invalid proof, are both refused at propose() (actor_not_authenticated) and record nothing: propose() authenticates the actor's proof over the exact request bytes. What this does NOT claim: a valid proof presented by the wrong party (a genuinely compromised credential) is indistinguishable at this layer — that limitation stands, stated in the engine's strength statement.
controls.name: unauthenticated_actor_proposal_refused
controls.observed: propose(bare actor)=refusal:actor_not_authenticated; propose(registered name, bad proof)=refusal:actor_not_authenticated; requests_recorded=0

controls.expected: A read of the sensitive-classification object by a principal without the reader_sensitive role (presenting its own valid proof), and a read with no identity at all, are both refused (read_not_authorized), and both refusals stand in the read audit. In v0.2 query() took no identity and served a state digest to any caller (Nov 9 comparison, V12: NOT_SUPPORTED).
controls.name: unauthorized_sensitive_read_refused_and_audited

controls.expected: A read of the sensitive object by the registered sensitive reader, presenting a valid proof over the read, is served as a query view of the classified state, and the served read stands in the read audit: authorization gates the read, and the audit covers both outcomes.
controls.name: authorized_sensitive_read_served_and_audited
controls.observed: query(authorized reader) kind=query_view; classification=sensitive; digest_matches=True; read_served_entries=1

adversarial_tests.claim: execute() re-checks the request actor's current authorization as it re-checks the approver's: an actor withdrawn before execution authorizes no effect; a current actor's request still executes; withdrawal after the effect neither rolls it back nor invalidates its receipt.

controls.expected: A request proposed by a registered actor, approved and released, whose actor is then withdrawn before execution, refuses at execute() (actor_no_longer_authorized) with no effect and no receipt: execute() re-checks the actor's CURRENT authorization. In v0.3 this request committed (outside finding, codexmainbizmac, 2026-11-10).
controls.name: withdrawn_actor_execution_refused

controls.expected: The same request shape with the actor still registered and active executes and is receipted: the actor-currency check refuses withdrawn actors, not current ones.
controls.name: current_actor_execution_commits

controls.expected: Withdrawing the actor after its effect committed does not roll the effect back, and the issued receipt still verifies: currency is checked where the effect is authorized, at execution, not retroactively.
controls.name: actor_withdrawal_after_effect_no_rollback

tests.claim: Query evidence and update evidence are different record kinds with different bindings; neither substitutes for the other. Scope note: that ordinary queries are unreceipted is this fixture's design convention for reads of standard-classification objects, not a universal security law — a disclosure-sensitive read can itself be consequential under a real policy, and in v0.3 a sensitive read is authorized and audited (see A3).

controls.expected: Two queries matching current state create query views and no receipts; the one authorized mutation produces a settlement receipt whose request digest differs from every query-view digest.
controls.name: queries_create_no_receipt_mutation_receipt_is_distinct

controls.expected: A query view relabeled as a settlement receipt fails independent verification: the view carries no request binding at all (verifier code: unknown_request), so a query/view digest cannot be substituted for the mutation's authoritative transition receipt.
controls.name: relabeled_query_view_fails_receipt_verification

tests.claim: A lost acknowledgment leaves the effect UNKNOWN_EFFECT until independent readback; reconciliation resolves it from the record and never authorizes a second mutation on the strength of the lost response.

controls.expected: Effect commits; acknowledgment is lost, so the caller's status is UNKNOWN_EFFECT; readback reconciliation returns the standing receipt and the effect stands applied exactly once in this fixture's store.
controls.name: lost_ack_reconciles_by_readback_effect_applied_once

controls.expected: A second, different mutation presented under the same idempotency key — the 'no response was seen, so send another' move — is refused; no second effect is authorized on the basis of a lost response.
controls.name: second_mutation_under_same_idempotency_key_refused

tests.claim: Revoking an upstream authority contests derived state built on it through DECLARED dependencies, prevents new reliance on the revoked request, and leaves history and unrelated activity intact.

controls.expected: Revoking upstream A (history and A's receipt preserved, nothing erased) flags declared dependent D as contested, refuses new reliance on A (dependency_revoked), and still permits unrelated authorized activity.
controls.name: revocation_flags_declared_dependents_blocks_new_reliance_allows_unrelated

controls.expected: LIMIT, on the record: a write whose payload copies the revoked upstream's output but declares no dependence executes undetected. Dependents are found through declared dependence (or independent discoverability in a real system), never by universal tracing. This control passes by demonstrating the limit, not by denying it.
controls.name: undeclared_dependence_limit_demonstrated

tests.claim: In v0.3 the effect store is mediated at its own boundary: the only write path is the governed dispatch, and a bypass route's write is refused by the store itself, leaving state unchanged and a record of the attempt. (In v0.1/v0.2 the same write landed; T6 then passed by demonstrating the gap. The expectation changed because the semantics changed — that is what a new kit version means.)

controls.expected: A write through the gate produces a receipt, and the observer comparison (store history vs receipt ledger) reports no unreceipted mutations.
controls.name: gated_write_receipted_observer_clean

controls.expected: MEDIATION AT THE STORE (v0.3 correction of the v0.1/v0.2 coverage gap): a write through a route not wired to the gate is refused BY THE EFFECT STORE ITSELF (ungoverned_write) — the store accepts writes only under the dispatch capability the governed path mints. State still holds the gated value, the refused attempt stands in the store's boundary log, and the observer comparison stays clean because no ungoverned mutation exists to flag. Scope: API-level mediation inside a single-process fixture; it governs every write route this fixture exposes and claims nothing against in-process introspection of the fixture's own memory.
controls.name: bypass_refused_at_store_state_unchanged
controls.observed: bypass_landed=False; refusal=ungoverned_write; store_refusal=True; refused_attempts=[{'object': 'obj-x', 'via': 'direct', 'request_id': None}]; observer_flags=[]; receipts=1

tests.strength: Local record-layer strength: a self-contained fixture engine in this kit implements the claimed semantics. A pass establishes that the semantics are coherent and reproducible against frozen inputs. It establishes nothing about any deployed system; run the same cases against a real stack under Issue #31 to test production behavior. This test measures mediation at the fixture store's boundary; it does not establish that every ungated action in any real system is prevented — that requires the store in that system to be mediated the same way, which is a property to examine there, not a conclusion to import from here.
